caption: The drawing depicts fragments of a woven textile featuring rectangular sections with complex patterns rendered in red, green, blue, and white. The largest piece is positioned centrally and consists of alternating horizontal bands, each showcasing different patterns: one band displays large eight-pointed stars within green, another shows a blue ground with intricate floral motifs, and another causes red to dominate with various floral and star shapes. In the lower right section, one red area contains white text that reads "ANDREW L. TRUMP DAMASK COVERLET MANUFACTURER HANOVER YORK COUNTY 1846." Near the lower edge, there is a linen fringe. To the upper right, there is a smaller red section with a white floral motif, bordered by a slender green strip at the bottom. To the upper left, another fragment shows a prominent eight-pointed star in green and white centered in its own rectangular space above a blue floral motif band. The woven textile pieces are displayed on a neutral, light tan background, and the composition provides a clear view of the textile pieces’ edges, some of which are frayed. The words "EVA WILSON" appear printed in green ink below the left side of the large textile piece.
title: Damask Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
